messages:
ana: Quick question — planning a sharded canary experiment for the new llama-compat model. Thinking deterministic shard routing by user_id so we can guarantee a stable cohort across rollouts. Anyone seen issues with sticky routing + autoscaling?

mike: sticky by user_id is fine, but we need to be explicit about bucketization (buckets vs percent). we use murmur3 -> 0..999 buckets in other services.

jin: watch out for cross-account routing: enterprise customers want per-tenant isolation. if a tenant has high QPS we shouldn't place them entirely in a 5% variant and blow their quota.

ana: @jin good call — we should support "tenant override" or quotas per-variant-per-tenant. does console UI surface that?

ana: also thinking about guards: automatic rollback if 5xxs or latency regresses by X% in last 5m. telemetry hooks need to be part of experiment definition.

samir: from infra side: autoscaling can create noisy neighbors if a variant spikes. we should allow variant-level capacity reservations for Dedicated customers. fallback routing to control when capacity low.

liz: UX note — when creating experiment in Console, showing a live predicted traffic distribution (buckets -> clients affected) helps. people get confused when they pick "5%" vs "50 buckets".

mike: API debate: should the control-plane store full routing policy (hash alg, key, buckets, sticky TTL) or keep it lightweight and push resolved routing to edge? pros/cons: storing full policy is easier for audits and rollbacks; pushing config to edge reduces runtime dependence on control plane.

jin: prefer storing policy in control plane and pushing configs to edge. we already have config-sync for model variants. keeps audit-history + we can diff policies for postmortems.

samir: edge push + local evaluation is fine, but require versioned policy id in token so we can trace which policy evaluated each request (for telemetry).

ana: sample experiment config I sketched (for the API/console):
```json
{
  "kind": "experiment",
  "id": "exp-2026-05-shard-test",
  "variants": [
    {"id": "control", "weight": 950},
    {"id": "llama-v2-small", "weight": 50}
  ],
  "routing": {
    "strategy": "shard",
    "key": "user_id",
    "hash": "murmur3",
    "buckets": 1000,
    "sticky_ttl_seconds": 2592000
  },
  "guards": {
    "rollback_on": {
      "p50_latency_ms": {"increase_pct": 30, "window_seconds": 300},
      "error_rate": {"absolute_pct": 1.0, "window_seconds": 120}
    },
    "capacity_fallback": "control",
    "per_tenant_variant_quota": {"enabled": true, "max_qps": 200}
  },
  "telemetry": {"emit_policy_id": true, "metric_tags": ["experiment_id","variant_id","policy_id"]}
}
```

liz: looks great. UI questions: 1) how to present sticky TTL? 2) default guard thresholds? we probably want sane defaults but allow advanced mode.

mike: agree defaults: rollback on 2x error rate or 25% latency reg vs baseline in 5m. expose advanced toggles in console.

ana: runtime concern — when we route by shard and a variant is unavailable (OOM/scale-down), we need immediate fallback. That fallback must be deterministic and signal telemetry that fallback happened.

samir: deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for exp-2026-05-shard-test -> variant=llama-v2-small (5%) :rocket:

deploy-bot: Policy pushed to edges: policy_id=pol_20260501_17 v=1.

jin: action items: (1) API: add policy_id + emit_policy_id to telemetry (2) Console: show estimated user count impacted for bucket sizes and provide "per-tenant quota" toggle (3) Infra: implement capacity_fallback path + variant reservations for Dedicated. i'll make PRs.

ana: thanks everyone — i'll update the Console experiment wizard mock with the new fields and default guard presets. will ping when ready for review. :thumbsup:
